the polarization effects provide substantial enhancements of the sensitivities to the Z-Z’ mixing angles in the \chi-model, the \psi-model, the \eta-model and the left–right model.
the polarization effects on W bosons and beam polarizations provide the strict constraints on Z-Z' mixing angle and the asymmetry variable.
the polarization effects are important to study the Z-Z' model.

the polarization effects on W bosons pair productions with the Z' boson.
the polarization effects of the e^+^e^- -> W^-W^- process in presence of the extra Z' boson at the linear collider.
the polarization effects in the W boson pair production at the LC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the \sigma_{LL,RR}^{unpol}, \sigma_{LR}^{unpol, pol}, A_{LR}, A_{RL}, A_{RL}^{\rm pol, unpol}, and A_{LR}^{\rm unpol, pol} are the most sensitive observables to the Z-Z'mixing angles in the models considered here.
the polarization effect is very important for the study of the extra gauge boson at LC.
the polarization effects on \sigma_{LL}, \sigma_{LR}, \sigma_{RL} and the beam polarization asymmetries are the most promising tools to determine the mixing angles in the Z-Z' sector.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the polarization effects on e^+e^-\rightarrow W^+W^-\ process are very important in the search of the new physics beyond the standard model.
the polarization effects are quite important in the study of the extra neutral boson and the beam polarization is very useful for the study of the mixing angles.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the polarizations of W bosons and beam polarizations can play a significant role in probing the Z-Z' mixings at the LC.
the polarization effects are crucial for the study of the Z-Z' mixings and the beam polarization asymmetries are very useful for the study of new physics.
